task_contract.anchor_definition: The anchor is the first target-specific value-construction function on the dynamic behavior chain: the earliest function, after routing and input preparation, whose own body constructs the target observable value rather than merely collecting inputs, dispatching control, packaging the result, or emitting it to the sink or fetch call.

runtime_boundary.event_plane: DOM submit event on the export form

evidence: The DevTools-visible JavaScript corpus is a single obfuscated bundle and no source map is exposed to the agent.
The target field name 'query_payload' is assembled from string fragments at the sink, so direct literal search is insufficient.
The fetch URL and X-Query-Payload header name are also assembled from string fragments, obscuring the network request destination.
The export route normalizes and projects click-time form state before the value constructor receives it.
A 32-slot reducer factory builds many slot-compatible sibling reducers; only the live slot value constructor feeds the target field.

The submit path crosses delegated form handling, action routing, value normalization, asynchronous staging, transit/middleware accumulation, projection lattice construction, request transform encoding, dynamic sink wrapping and fetch header assignment.
The same submit interaction emits non-target report.shadow/report.preview objects carrying shadow_key/preview_key values before the target report.export object.
The deployed bundle also contains 44 off-chain decoy reducers and 25 vendor-like modules that execute or remain reachable-looking without feeding the target query_payload field.
The target value is separated from the click by Promise, microtask, timer, animation-frame and MutationObserver boundaries.
The projection tuple is rebuilt from transit and middleware state before the encoder receives it.
The final sink receives an already-transformed value, so sink inspection or fetch interception alone does not identify the construction site.

behavior_category.subtype: click-time form and configuration transform value written to request header
behavior_category.reason: The observable value is a deterministic transform of form fields, route/config state and projection state, written to the X-Query-Payload header of a fetch request. It is not a state-only code, browser fingerprint or static signature.

near_categories.why_not: The output is not console-only; the same value is also assigned to a fetch request header field, making this a request transformation case.
The output has no cryptographic proof/seal semantics; it is a deterministic transform key, not a signed token.
The chain uses local DOM/form state, not browser/device capability collection as the target behavior.
